title: Two Things That Explain Most Things
subtitle: 引力物理 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 引力物理（宇宙探索·引力与物理）
meta: 主题语境：引力物理（宇宙探索·引力与物理）　|　核心词汇：source　|　正文 354 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 source 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: Gravity is the cheapest ① source of energy we have, and the least noticed. Every river runs downhill because of it, and so does every apple, though nobody wrote that down for a very long time. The ② source of the stream behind my grandfather's house is a spring two kilometres up the mountain, and once a year he walked there to clear the leaves away.

At school we are forever told to ③ name our source — the book, the author, the year. In science the rule is stricter still, because a figure without a source is only an opinion wearing a coat. Our teacher insisted that we record where every number came from: errors caught ④ at source are cheap, and errors found six months later are not.

The Sun is the obvious example. Its light comes from fusion deep in its core, and almost nothing we use is truly separate from it: coal, wind and hydroelectric power are all, in the end, energy ⑤ sourced from the same star at different removes. Every source of light we can see at night is enormous, and every one of them is very far away.

Yet the ⑥ source of the confusion in our class was not energy but weight. We had been told that weight and mass are not the same thing, and six of us simply refused to believe it: my own weight, I argued, cannot change from one street to the next. My teacher asked mildly what keeps us on the ground, and why the attraction differs slightly between the equator and the pole. Every source of error, he added, is a lesson in disguise.

So we spent two lessons reading original papers instead of the textbook. I learned that a ⑦ source older than your teacher is not necessarily wiser, and that a second-hand ⑧ source should always be chased back to the first one. Now I ask three questions of every number I meet: who measured it, how, and when. No honest answer travels far without its ⑨ source, which is why my grandfather's only question each spring was whether the ⑩ source up the mountain was still running.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: B. n. （河流的）源头；发源地
D. v. 获得；取自（be sourced from）
E. 固定搭配：energy/light source 能源／光源
F. 固定搭配：at source 在源头；从根本上
G. 固定搭配：source of information 信息来源（第一手／二手）
H. 固定搭配：name/cite one's source 注明出处

items.q: The source of the stream behind my grandfather's house
forever told to name our source
errors caught at source are cheap
energy sourced from the same star
the source of the confusion in our class
a source older than your teacher
a second-hand source should always be chased back
whether the source up the mountain was still running

answers.why: source of energy 是固定搭配，指能源／能量的来源，此处说引力是最廉价的能源。
the source of the stream 后接山上的泉眼，是“河流的源头”。
name one's source 意为“注明出处”，后面括号里的书名、作者、年份正是要注明的内容。
at source 意为“在源头处、从根本上”，此处说错误在源头被发现时代价最小。
be sourced from＋来源，是动词“取自、来源于”，说明各种能源最终都来自同一颗恒星。
the source of the confusion 意为“困惑的根源”，指同学们误会的原因。
此处 source 指信息来源，a source older than your teacher 意为“比老师更古老的资料”。
同样是信息来源，二手资料应当追回到一手。
without its source 指没有来源、出处，强调任何数据都必须交代来路。
山上那处仍在流淌的 source 仍是“源头”，与第 2 题首尾呼应。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 这条小溪的源头是山上一处泉眼。（source n.）
老师要求我们注明每一条资料的出处。（name one's source）
错误在源头处被发现的代价最小。（at source）
我们使用的几乎所有能源最终都来自同一颗恒星。（be sourced from）
我们班困惑的根源不是能量，而是重量。（the source of）
如果是二手资料，我总会去找第一手的。（source n.）
answers: The source of this stream is a spring up the mountain.
The teacher asked us to name our source for every figure.
Errors caught at source cost the least.
Almost all the energy we use is sourced from the same star.
The source of the confusion in our class was not energy but weight.
If it is a second-hand source, I always go back to the first one.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 source 的 3 种不同用法；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: Gravity is the cheapest source of energy we have, though it is the least noticed.
The source of the stream behind my grandfather's house is a spring two kilometres up the mountain.
Every figure needs a source: errors caught at source are cheap, and those found six months later are not.
Coal, wind and falling water are all, in the end, energy sourced from the same star.
Later I learned that weight depends on attraction and mass, which settled the source of our class confusion.
A source older than my teacher is not always wiser, so I chase every second-hand source back to the first.
